Triage: lands in `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` (`readonlyStripWarning`, plus the unverified `runtimeOwnedStripWarning` sibling on the insert side) ⇒ `domain:engine-core`, `pm:queue`, type Bug. Both defects are one string + its pin tests; the card's own scope note (keep `warn` level, keep naming field/consequence/true remedy, do not re-open #8141) is the acceptance frame.

Dispatch constraints for the executing seat (#6019):
- **Dispatch only after #8141's PR merges** — its acceptance bar pins this line as unchanged-in-wording for the cases that still print, so a wording change now collides with an in-flight pin by design.
- **Hard serial vs #8215** (same file) — never the same batch.
- Verify the insert-side sibling claim (`strictReadonlyWrites` discharge on `insert`, #5126/#5503) before wording it — it is flagged unverified in the card.

Size/model suggestion: S-but-judgment-in-wording ⇒ M treatment, sonnet/opus at seat's discretion.

### Serial constraints — derived from real diffs

`rule-validator.ts` is **free**: #8216 landed at `e50e479ed` (21:51Z) and released it; nothing else is in flight in this lane. #7501's reservation is on `record-validator.ts`, a different file, and is `pm:blocked` with no branch.

## ⚠️ You will break a pin that landed 20 minutes ago. That is the intended handoff, not an accident.

#8216 (#8141) deliberately asserted `readonlyStripWarning` **byte-identical** — `toBe` against the exported message, plus the emitted level — because its own acceptance bar required proving it had **narrowed** the warning rather than deleted it. I ruled that PR's wording question as *"leave the string alone; #8214 decides the text once, on its own evidence, with a pin that is free to change because it was written for that purpose."*

⭐ So: **update that pin, do not work around it.** And keep what it was protecting — the level stays `warn` (its docblock argues the level so real forgery attempts stay visible), and the surviving line must still name the field, the consequence, and a remedy that is **true for the case that prints**.

⛔ **Do not re-open #8141.** The addressing `id` no longer reaches this message at all. If your change would make it print again for a by-id address write, you have gone wrong.

## Defect 1 — "COMMITTED WITHOUT IT" is false under `strictReadonlyWrites`

Measured on the card: `refusedCode: ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED`, `driverWrites: 0`, `warnLines: 1`, `claimsCommitted: true`. The strip logs from inside `stripReadonlyFields`; `assertNoStrictDrops()` throws **afterwards, before any driver call**. So a strict caller is told the update was committed without the field while nothing was written — the #4632 shape inverted, and a reader debugging from the log alone hunts for a row that was never touched.

⛔ **The fix is not to drop the warning in strict mode.** The forgery signal is still wanted; what must stop is the **claim of a commit**. Whether that means the message learns the strict flag, or the log moves after the decision, or the strict path gets its own line, is yours to choose and to argue in the PR — ⛔ but say which you picked and why the other options are worse.

⭐ **Verify the insert side too.** The card names `runtimeOwnedStripWarning` as carrying the same "COMMITTED WITHOUT IT" claim while `insert` also discharges `strictReadonlyWrites` (#5126 / #5503), and explicitly marks it **unverified**. Measure it; if it reproduces, it is the same string family and belongs in this card. If it does **not** reproduce, say so with the measurement — a negative result is a result.

## Defect 2 — the remedy names `isSystem` but never `preserveAudit`

`stripReadonlyFields` honours `context.preserveAudit` (#3493) — a **whitelist**, narrower than `isSystem` by construction — while the message offers only the blanket exemption. Its own runtime-owned twin names **both**, and a test pins that it does. So two sibling messages disagree about the remedy set for the same pair of exemptions, and an import that forgot the flag is steered to the strictly-worse posture — the identical failure #8141 just fixed one remedy over.

⚠️ **Be precise about what `preserveAudit` actually covers before you advertise it.** It is `AUDIT_TIMELINE_FIELDS` plus any non-`system` field — and that second limb is itself defective (**#8215**, `pm:blocked`: it currently sweeps in a platform object's primary key). ⛔ Do not describe the whitelist in a way that will become false when #8215 lands, and ⛔ do not fix #8215 here. The card's own question is the right one: **does the audit-family case deserve a targeted remedy sentence rather than a blanket one?** Answer it in the PR.

## Two hazards this seat learned today — both are dispatch conditions, not suggestions

1. ⛔ **Never `git add -A`.** Per #8218, `check:type-check-debt` writes `tsconfig.debt-remeasure.json` into a **tracked package directory that is not gitignored**; one blanket add commits it. Stage explicit paths. I will read the PR's file list at acceptance.
2. ⛔ **Commit before you reverse-verify.** With no commit on the branch, `git checkout <branch> -- <file>` and `git checkout origin/main -- <file>` resolve to the **same tree**, and the restore silently destroys your fix. Push early — even a WIP scaffold — then `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` and `git diff --stat HEAD` both mean what you want.

## Gates & deliverable

Derive with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs <changed paths>`; ⛔ never hand-enumerate, and re-derive if the surface changes. `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` needs a **built** closure. ⛔ Baselines may only shrink. Report each gate's exit status and state plainly that nothing was raised.

Changeset: observable log behaviour changes ⇒ a `patch` changeset, not `skip-changeset`.

Draft PR, first line `Fixes #8214`. ⛔ Do not flip to ready, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM does that after reading each job's own `conclusion`.

## ACCEPTED on substance — PR #8250. ⏳ Ready-flip held until every job is `completed` (run started 23:33Z; 11 still `in_progress`, zero failures — ⛔ not green).

`domain:engine-core` seat (#6019). Verified independently, not from the PR body: the **file list** (7 files, all `packages/objectql` + the changeset, ⛔ no stray `tsconfig.debt-remeasure.json` — the #8218 tripwire was *checked* this time rather than survived by luck) and the **`engine.ts` diff**, which was the one conditional fence in the dispatch.

### The fence held, and the justification was measured rather than asserted

`engine.ts` is exactly three call sites threading `strictReadonlyWrites`, plus comments. Nothing else moved. And the claim that all three are load-bearing is not prose: reverting `engine.ts` alone produced **3 failures, one per threaded line**. ⭐ The multi-branch one is the one that matters — a fix threaded only through the by-id site would have left `updateMany` still telling a refused caller its write had been committed, and nothing in the card would have caught it.

## ⭐ The C1 result is the most valuable thing here, and it corrects something *I* said

> *a pin written as `expect(warns).toEqual([readonlyStripWarning(...)])` computes its expectation from the **same** reverted composer, so both sides move together and the pin stays green*

That is a general defect class, not a detail of this PR: **a pin that derives its expectation from the code under test cannot detect a change in that code.** It verifies that the strip passes the right *arguments*; it says nothing about the *text*. The literal assertions (`not.toContain('COMMITTED WITHOUT IT')`, `toContain('REFUSED ENTIRELY')`) are what actually caught the revert — which is why both kinds belong in the file rather than only the tidier one.

⛔ **And it means my own ACCEPT on #8141 was wrong on this point.** I wrote there:

> *the surviving WARN is asserted with `toBe` against the **exported** `readonlyStripWarning` … A reworded line fails.*

**It would not have.** A reword of the composer moves both sides of that assertion together and the pin stays green. What #8216's pin really protected was the argument set and — separately and genuinely — the emitted **level**, which is asserted against a literal and does still catch a downgrade. I praised a guarantee the test did not provide, and the dev of this card measured it instead of inheriting it. Correcting it here, in the same channel where I said it. ⚠️ Anyone auditing the #8141 thread should read this paragraph as amending that one.

## Defect 1 — the shape chosen, and the two rejections

**The strip learns the flag.** Correct, and for the reason given: the seam that composes the sentence is the seam that must know what the sentence describes. Both rejections are argued on consequences rather than taste —

- *move the log after the decision* would delete the line entirely under strict, which the dispatch explicitly forbade: the forgery signal is the half worth keeping;
- *a second strict-only line* leaves the false sentence already printed, so a reader grepping `COMMITTED WITHOUT IT` still gets the lie, and two composers must then be kept in sync forever.

Keeping all wording in one exported composer is also what makes the pins possible at all.

⭐ **The insert-side half was filed UNVERIFIED and you measured it instead of assuming it.** It reproduces — same code, same `driverCreates 0`, same false sentence, same sequencing. That is the right disposition: an unverified claim inherited from a card is not evidence, and had it *not* reproduced, saying so would have been just as valuable.

## Defect 2 — you answered the card's question better than it was asked

The card asked *targeted or blanket?*. You returned **targeted and derived**: the remedy is gated on `isPreservableUnderAudit` — the same predicate the strip consults a line earlier — rather than on prose describing the whitelist. Three consequences, all of which I would have missed if I had ruled the shape myself:

1. **A blanket sentence would be false for real fields.** Measured on `organization_id`: `preserveAudit` is set, the field is stripped anyway, the line prints. Advertising `preserveAudit` there is #8141's own defect one exemption over — a caller steered to a posture that does not help. Withheld, and pinned.
2. **It cannot go stale when #8215 lands.** A sentence *describing* the whitelist becomes false the day that predicate narrows; a sentence *gated on* it narrows automatically. ⭐ This is the right answer to a hazard I raised in the dispatch as a thing to avoid — you removed the possibility rather than dodging it.
3. **It resolves the sibling disagreement at the root** — both messages now read one predicate, so they cannot disagree by construction. Stronger than copying one message's wording into the other, which is what the card literally suggested.

The safety-by-position argument checks out too: a field kept by `preserveAudit` never reaches the log, so any field that does reach it with the flag on is one the whitelist refused.

## Scope and the standing hazards

⛔ `record-validator.ts` untouched (#7501's reservation) · ⛔ `isPreservableUnderAudit` untouched, so **#8215 stays blocked and unaffected** · ⛔ no `packages/spec`, no `content/docs/**`, no ADR, nothing release-owned. The #8141 pins were **updated in place**, not worked around, and its counter-cases — a forged field riding along with the address must still warn — are still green, now in strict mode too.

⚠️ **`check:objectui-pin-fresh` exited 1 locally and `Console Pin Freshness` came back `success` in CI at 23:33:45Z** — the second instance of that disagreement in this lane today. Your read that it is unrelated is right; ⛔ the local exit code still is not a fact about CI, in either direction. The gate job is the authority.

Next: each job's own `conclusion`, then ready + auto-merge SQUASH.
